title: Why Does One Volcano Ooze and Another Explode?
description: The surprising difference between gentle lava rivers and huge explosions.
narration: Why does one volcano gently ooze while another blows its top? Deep down, rock gets so hot that some of it melts into thick, flowing magma. Magma is lighter than the rock around it, so it rises. Thin, runny magma lets gas slip out, so it simply flows. Thick, sticky magma traps the gas, and pressure builds until boom. So Earth has both exploding volcanoes and slow rivers of lava.

claims.sentence: Deep down, rock gets so hot that some of it melts into thick, flowing magma.
claims.quote: some rocks slowly melt and become a thick flowing substance called magma

claims.sentence: Magma is lighter than the rock around it, so it rises.
claims.quote: Since it is lighter than the solid rock around it, magma rises and collects in magma chambers.

claims.sentence: Thin, runny magma lets gas slip out, so it simply flows.
claims.quote: If magma is thin and runny, gases can escape easily from it. When this type of magma erupts, it flows out of the volcano.

claims.sentence: Thick, sticky magma traps the gas, and pressure builds until boom.
claims.quote: If magma is thick and sticky, gases cannot escape easily. Pressure builds up until the gases escape violently and explode.

claims.sentence: So Earth has both exploding volcanoes and slow rivers of lava.
claims.quote: volcanoes that explode with ash and gas, and volcanoes that have slow rivers of melted rock
